scope: two real server players, one native rendering client; the captain clicks cache interfaces with the real mouse and the guest sends the packets a second client would send

checks.detail: guest published as wire pid 2 on hull view 1; harness projection put its model at screen (422,252) and a real mouse move to that point put element 805308158 in the client's own world pick set (picked=True)

checks.name: Edit-navigator grants and revokes navigation by mouse alone
checks.detail: Real mouse only: crew tab -> Players -> right-click (645, 407) -> left-click the 'Edit-navigator' row at (645, 422) -> left-click the guest at [412, 281] (the client's own pick reports picked=True there), twice. vessel_stat 11 navigator mask 0 -> 2 -> 0 (peer pid 1, bit 2); peer role varbit 19233 3 -> 6 -> 3; ToriRSServer_VesselCanNavigate False -> True -> False. The control image is the same IF3 target mechanism on an inventory item ('Use Coins'), whose priority is a real op slot.

checks.name: Edit-navigator grant and revoke reach vessel_stat 11, role 6 and helm permission
checks.detail: vessel_stat 11 navigator mask 0 -> 2 -> 0 (peer pid 1, bit 2); peer role varbit 19233 3 -> 6 -> 3; ToriRSServer_VesselCanNavigate False -> True -> False. Driven by harness 'peer target', which puts the same component and the same player index into the same OPPLAYERT the armed click above sends: both halves now name the player by the GPI index the server published (ToriRSServer_WirePlayerIndex — content_test_sailing.c's 'peer target' writes it, handle_opplayert matches it). This row is the server-side control for the mouse row above: the row above proves the client arms and sends it, this one proves the handler grants on it. The captain's chat carries the content's own 'You grant/remove <name>'s navigation permission' lines.

checks.name: Board-friend: the guest boards the captain's boat by name
checks.detail: The guest's real OPLOC3 on the Pandemonium gangplank ran [oploc3,sailing_gangplank_embark] -> ~sailing_board_friend and PARKED on p_namedialog (peer active_script=1, execution=7 = SSVM_NAMEDIALOG); the harness answered with RESUME_P_NAMEDIALOG "fin3dock" and the script resumed and ran to completion (script=0). The guest went from 3069,2987 level 0 view 0 to 6403,66 level 1 view 1, which is the captain's hull view 1 and the captain's own deck plane 1. Captain's owned-boat registration (sailing_boat_1_owned=1, sailing_boat_1_port=1, hull cargo slot 1, dock_id 1) is read in the CAPTAIN's script context, which is what the vessel_* opcodes now answer for; the client's own world pick reports picked=True on the guest's model. For the deck picture the guest was then walked one tile to 6404,68 (separated=True), because VesselBoardPlayer lands it on the captain's own tile and the two models coincide exactly.

checks.name: boarding by name grants no navigation permission
checks.detail: peer role varbit sailing_sidepanel_player_role = 3 (the cache's passenger rung 3 -- see docs/sailing_validation/social/roles-results.json), ToriRSServer_VesselCanNavigate=False, vessel_stat 11 navigator mask 0 -> 0

checks.name: the guest opens the cargo hold with a real OPLOC on the deck's hold loc
checks.detail: the hold loc sits at deck 6404,65 -- ~sailing_facilities_place puts sailing_boat_cargo_hold_regular_2x5 at the hull frame's base+(4,1) for config 2, and the guest's OPLOC1 walked it from 6404,68 to 6404,66. At privacy 0 (Navigators) a non-navigator guest is refused: mainmodal=0, cargo=False. At privacy 1 (All players) the same click opens the native hold: mainmodal=943 (943), cargo=True. The capture is the CAPTAIN's screen -- the guest has no client of its own, so its open hold is the server reading above, not a rendered panel; what the picture carries is the guest standing at the hold on the captain's deck.
